default.note: Changing a globe is normal use of the fitting, not electrical work. Switch off at the wall and let hot globes cool first.
A battery-only alarm isn't connected to mains wiring, so you can fit or replace it yourself. Check your state's smoke-alarm rules for rentals and sales — some require interconnected hardwired alarms.

QLD.note: Photoelectric alarms powered by a 10-year non-removable battery can be installed yourself. From 1 January 2027 every Queensland home needs interconnected photoelectric alarms in each bedroom, connecting hallways and every storey.

default.note: Plugging an appliance into an existing power point is normal use. Adding or moving the power point is licensed electrical work.
Replacing or adding a power point — even like-for-like — is electrical installation work that needs a licensed electrician in every state and territory.

VIC.note: Energy Safe Victoria: electrical work isn't a DIY job, even for small jobs such as changing power points or light switches.

QLD.note: Queensland's Electrical Safety Office lists installing a power point as licensed electrical work. Fines for individuals can reach $40,000.

NSW.note: In NSW a licence is needed for any electrical wiring work, regardless of cost or type. Your electrician lodges a CCEW when finished.

WA.note: WA's advice is 'never replace fittings and switches yourself'. Use a licensed electrician.

default.note: Replacing a light switch is electrical installation work that needs a licensed electrician in every state and territory.

VIC.note: Energy Safe Victoria names changing light switches as work that isn't DIY.

QLD.note: Queensland's Electrical Safety Office lists replacing a switch as licensed electrical work.

WA.note: WA: 'never replace fittings and switches yourself'.

default.note: Light fittings and downlights are wired into the lighting circuit, so replacing them needs a licensed electrician in every state.

QLD.note: Queensland's Electrical Safety Office lists replacing a batten holder with a light fitting as licensed electrical work.

default.note: Installing a ceiling fan connects to fixed wiring and needs a licensed electrician in every state. You can assemble it before the electrician arrives.

QLD.note: Queensland's Electrical Safety Office lists replacing a light fitting with a ceiling fan as licensed electrical work.

default.note: Hardwired (mains-powered) smoke alarms connect to fixed wiring, so they must be installed by a licensed electrician.
Hardwired appliances must be connected by a licensed electrician. You can position and fit the appliance — just not make the connection.

QLD.note: Queensland's Electrical Safety Office: hardwired appliances must be connected by a licensed electrician. Fitting a wall oven into its cabinet without connecting it is not electrical work.

default.note: We couldn't confirm your state's position from the regulator. Don't assume it's allowed — ask your electrical regulator, or have an electrician do it.

QLD.note: Queensland's Electrical Safety Office lists replacing a plug on the end of an extension lead, and constructing an extension lead, as licensed electrical work.

default.note: We couldn't confirm a homeowner exemption from your regulator. Check with them before doing any plumbing work yourself.

QLD.note: Replacing a jumper valve or washer in a tap is on the QBCC's list of unregulated plumbing work.

WA.note: Since March 2024, owners can maintain or repair a tap (not thermostatic mixing taps).

VIC.note: Tap washers and other minor tap repairs in a home are exempt from Victoria's plumbing licensing rules.

NSW.note: An owner-occupier may repair a tap in their home (not thermostatic mixing or tempering valves).

TAS.note: Repairing tapware on your own property is low-risk work owners can do.

default.note: Replacing a whole tap or mixer means disconnecting and reconnecting the water supply — licensed plumbing work. The homeowner exemptions cover repair only.

TAS.note: Tasmania lets owners repair or replace tapware like-for-like on their own property as low-risk work (vegetable-spray mixers excluded).

default.note: We couldn't confirm a homeowner exemption from your regulator. Check with them first.

QLD.note: Replacing a shower head is on the QBCC's unregulated plumbing work list.

WA.note: Owners can maintain, repair or replace a showerhead.

VIC.note: Changing over a water-efficient showerhead is exempt from Victoria's plumbing licensing rules.

NSW.note: NSW lets an owner-occupier repair a showerhead. Replacing one outright isn't clearly covered — check with NSW Fair Trading.

TAS.note: Owners can replace showerheads and shower hoses like-for-like on their own property.

default.note: We couldn't confirm a homeowner exemption from your regulator — treat it as licensed work unless they confirm otherwise.

QLD.note: Repairing or replacing the drop-valve washer, float-valve washer or suction-cup rubber in a toilet cistern is unregulated work.

WA.note: Owners can replace a cistern washer.

default.note: Replacing a toilet suite involves the water supply and the sewer connection — licensed plumbing work in every state.

NSW.note: NSW requires a licence for any plumbing work regardless of cost; individuals face fines of up to $22,000.

default.note: Connecting a dishwasher to the water supply and drain isn't on any state's homeowner exemption list we could confirm — use a licensed plumber.
Using a plunger on a blocked sink or basin is normal household maintenance. Opening up drains or using drain machines is licensed work.

WA.note: WA owners can clear a blocked fixture or waste pipe with a plunger.

QLD.note: Plunging is normal maintenance, and cleaning a ground-level trap grate is on the QBCC's unregulated list. Anything beyond the grate needs a plumber.

default.note: Replacing a hot water system is licensed plumbing work everywhere — and gas units also need a licensed gasfitter.
All gasfitting — pipework, installing or moving gas appliances, and installing a bayonet point — needs a licensed gasfitter in every state.

VIC.note: In Victoria, installing, moving or replacing a gas appliance needs a licensed gasfitter and always needs a compliance certificate.

default.note: Plugging a portable appliance into an existing bayonet is what bayonets are designed for. Installing the bayonet is licensed gasfitting. Some states restrict unflued gas heaters — check the heater is legal to use where you live.

Waterproofing is generally not licence-at-any-value work for a homeowner on their own home, but owner-builder value limits apply and the work must meet the National Construction Code (AS 3740). Any pipework needs a licensed plumber.

NSW.note: Contractor licences apply to waterproofing work for others over $5,000. On your own home, an owner-builder permit is needed over $10,000 if the work needs a DA or CDC. Must meet AS 3740.

QLD.note: Owners can do work on their own property valued up to $11,000 without a licence; above that needs an owner-builder permit. Must meet the building code.

VIC.note: Domestic building work on your own home over $20,000 needs an owner-builder certificate of consent. Must meet the building code.

default.note: Patching plasterboard is cosmetic work with no licence needed. Check for cables and pipes before cutting; repairs to either need a licensed electrician or plumber. If the wall might be asbestos-containing fibro, get it tested first.
Regrouting and replacing silicone is maintenance you can do yourself everywhere. If water is getting behind the tiles, the waterproofing may have failed; that needs more than new grout.
